item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.3
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 3

A guided setup. Setup now introduces each feature, asks for the permissions it needs at that step, and shows what is downloading at the bottom of every screen. You can try dictation before you finish, and open a sample meeting to see what a write-up looks like. Everyone sees it once after updating; what you already allowed and downloaded shows as Ready, and your settings stay as they are.

A consent reminder before notes. Before Tailwing takes notes on a call, it asks you to confirm that you are responsible for getting consent from everyone you take notes with. Tailwing sends that confirmation to us once, with the date, the app version and an ID for your Mac, so it is on file. Dictation doesn't need it.

Ask shows what it will assume. As you type a question, Tailwing underlines the meeting, the dates and the people it will look at. Click one to change it before you send. Where it can't tell which meeting or person you mean, it asks instead of guessing, and each answer starts with what it was based on.

Decisions in one place. View, Decisions lists every decision across your meetings, newest first, with the reason given in the meeting and a link to the moment it was made.

Projects. Tell Tailwing about your most important projects in setup, or add them on the new Projects page. Each project collects its decisions, open next steps and meetings in one place, and you can ask a question about that project alone. Setup can also list your recurring meetings so you can say which project each belongs to, and you can mark a meeting as a project's anchor. Sorting items into projects automatically is off for now; you can turn it on in Settings.

How You Run Meetings. A new page beside Decisions shows your last four weeks against the four before: your share of talk time, the questions you asked, how often you started while someone was mid-sentence, your longest stretch and the cues you saw most. The suggestion under each meeting is now labeled Try Next Time. All of it stays on your Mac.

Links to a moment. Copy a link to any transcript line, source line or flagged moment. Opening it shows that line in the transcript. Exports and AI tools carry the same links.

Anonymize covers everything you save. With Anonymize on, names and personal details are now replaced in the notes you save, copy, share, drag out or send, including PDF and Markdown files and next steps sent to Reminders, Things and Todoist. If they can't be replaced, nothing is saved or sent.

Share and drag. Share a note from the macOS Share menu, or drag it to Finder or Mail.

Usage numbers, if you choose. Setup asks whether Tailwing may send counts about how it is working on your Mac, such as whether setup finished. It is off until you say yes, it never includes anything you say, write or dictate, and Settings, Privacy shows exactly what was sent. The same screen has an optional question about what you do for work. Your answer stays on your Mac unless you share usage numbers, and then it is sent as one of nine fixed choices.

Rate a dictation. Each item in your dictation history has Good and Not good buttons, and Not good lets you say what went wrong. Ratings stay on your Mac. If you share usage numbers, each rating is also counted with the kind of app and the language, and never the words or the audio.

Update checks are counted. When Tailwing checks for an update, our site counts the check with the app's version and build number, so we can see how many Macs are on each version. Nothing else is sent, and if that address doesn't answer, Tailwing checks the original one.

More at home on the Mac. Complete menus with the standard keys, a Help menu, spell check in notes, Settings that follow Increase Contrast, and a quiet start at login. The interface is now translated in the places that were still in English.

Better write-ups of long meetings. Write-ups no longer present something reported from a paper or a dashboard as a decision the group made, they stay a readable length, and decisions and next steps now come through when you typed your own notes during the meeting.

Next steps say when nobody was named. When a meeting agrees a next step without saying who will do it, the write-up no longer guesses. The step shows "Who?" with the people in the meeting to choose from, and your choice stays if you regenerate the write-up.

Fixed. Dictation now types into Tailwing's own text boxes, such as a project's description, a note or the Ask box. Exported files no longer get a doubled extension. Undo while typing undoes your typing. Deleting a folder, a template or your dictation history asks first. Dictated text placed before a word is followed by a space. Private mode's one-time model download now covers live captions. Closing setup early no longer marks it finished.

Known issues. The selected row in Decisions and in the sidebar is hard to read on the blue highlight. After a call, your own voice can show as "Speaker 1" or your email address where your name should be. Ask reads what it will assume for questions in English only. Translations of the newest wording are awaiting review by native readers. The reason shown under a decision is often missing in long meetings.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.2
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 2

Setup that finishes by itself. Tailwing now downloads every model it needs on its own, shows how far along each one is, and tries again if a download stops. Dictation works as soon as its speech model is in, with no need to reopen the app. Settings, Models and Settings, Permissions use the same rows and the same words, and each opens with one line that says whether everything is ready.

Private mode from the first screen. If you choose Private mode during setup, Tailwing downloads its models once and then stays offline. If a model is missing later, Settings, Models says so and offers Download Once, which leaves Private mode on.

Better write-ups of long meetings. In meetings of 35 minutes and more, Tailwing now catches far more of the decisions and next steps, including the ones made late in the meeting.

One document for your notes. Your own lines stay as you wrote them, and the write-up fills in around them. Anything you type after the write-up is included the next time it's written. Exports, the folder and webhook files, the local API and AI tools all get the same document, and the local API marks which lines are yours.

A redesigned side panel. During a call it shows your notes with a strip of the transcript. After the call it shows the write-up, with Notes, Transcript and Ask a tap away.

Dictation can read your browser tab. In Chrome, Arc, Edge or Brave, dictation can also spell the names on the page you're typing into. It's off until you turn on "Also use the page in your browser tab" in Settings, Dictation. macOS asks to let Tailwing control your browser, which Tailwing uses only to check that no private window is open before it reads. Safari can't tell Tailwing whether a private window is open, so Tailwing never reads Safari pages.

Better speaker names on calls. When an invite lists the people on a call, it now limits how many voices Tailwing assigns to your microphone, so a short burst of speech is less likely to become an extra speaker. A name that sounds close to yours isn't offered as someone else, and a voice that thanks or greets someone is no longer taken to be that person.

Also new. Check for Updates is in the menu-bar menu. Speech runs on the Neural Engine by itself for English meetings on Macs that have one. Clearer wording across Settings and setup.

Fixed. Dictation keeps going if your input device changes while you hold the key. Dictation no longer pastes into a field that can't be described while a password field is in use elsewhere. Dictation never waits more than a second for names from the screen.

Known issues. Page reading in Arc, Edge and Brave has had only light testing. Translations of the newest wording are awaiting review by native readers. Features that use your own voice are not part of this beta.

item.title: Tailwing 1.1.0-beta.1
item.description:
Tailwing 1.1 Beta 1

A new start. Setup walks through the six things Tailwing does, one at a time: meeting notes, asking your meetings, dictation, privacy, your tools and languages. Each step asks for its permission where it's needed.

Encrypted on your Mac, audio included. Notes and transcripts were already encrypted on this Mac. Meeting audio is now encrypted as soon as the meeting is written up. A recovery code lets you open your notes on a new Mac after Migration Assistant or a restore from a backup; it's in Settings, Privacy, Your data.

AI tools are back. Claude and other AI tools read your meetings through the Tailwing app again, and only while you allow it: turn them on in Settings, Connections, AI tools.

Calls end better. When a call goes quiet, Tailwing asks before it stops. If a browser call it stopped picks up again, it asks whether to continue the last meeting.

Anonymize. The Pro feature that replaces names and personal details before anything leaves your Mac is now called Anonymize.

Coming next: more accurate dictation that spells the names on your screen, and sharper notes. Tell us what to fix first with Send Feedback in the Tailwing menu.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.8.2
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 8.2

Notes now stop by themselves when a browser call ends. After a Meet in Chrome, Tailwing could go on taking notes until you stopped it: Chrome kept hold of the microphone, and a normal room is rarely quiet enough for Tailwing to decide the call was over.

This version watches the same signal as the orange microphone dot in your menu bar, so leaving the call ends notes within seconds. If you were only stepping away, the call taking the microphone again within two minutes picks up the same meeting.

The AI tools connector is still paused, as in RC 8.1. It comes back in the next release.

item.title: Tailwing 1.0.0-rc.8.1
item.description:
Tailwing 1.0.0 RC 8.1

This release fixes rc.8, which some of you installed for a short time on 13 November.

rc.8 couldn't open an existing library after the update, so your meetings didn't appear and features that read them, such as import and dictation, stopped working. Nothing was lost: rc.8 stopped before changing anything. This version opens your library, encrypts your notes and transcripts on this Mac as rc.8 intended, and keeps every meeting.

rc.8 could also delete a writing model you had already downloaded and fetch it again. This version checks the file and keeps it when it matches.

Everything else in rc.8 is here: Private mode, encrypted notes and transcripts, the enforced list of what can leave this Mac, and the rest. The welcome screen loses its dot pattern.

One thing is paused in this version: the connector that lets Claude and other AI tools read your meetings. Now that the library is encrypted, the connector can't yet reach its key, so those tools will say they couldn't read the Tailwing library. Your meetings are unaffected. The connector comes back in the next release, reading through Tailwing itself.
